overview.background: Pathological Myopia is a severe form of nearsightedness that can lead to progressive vision loss if not detected early. Our project aims to address this challenge by leveraging machine learning to develop an advanced diagnostic system. This system will assist ophthalmologists in detecting the disease at an early stage, enabling timely intervention and management. We are a team of four dedicated Software Engineering students from Makerere University, driven by a passion for AI in healthcare and its transformative impact on medical diagnostics.
overview.data_collection: The data collection phase took place from September 2024 to November 2024. During this period, we collaborated with experienced ophthalmologists to gather a comprehensive dataset. This dataset consists of high-resolution eye scan images from various patients, ensuring diversity and reliability in training our machine learning model. Each image was carefully labeled and processed to enhance the accuracy of our diagnostic system.
overview.development: Once the data collection was complete, we transitioned into the development phase. Our primary focus was on analyzing the collected data, documenting key observations, and building a machine learning model capable of accurately diagnosing Pathological Myopia. Through extensive testing and refinement, we are working to enhance the system’s reliability. Additionally, we are preparing a detailed report that outlines our methodologies, results, and future improvements to ensure transparency and scientific rigor.
